title: South Korea launches joint inspection after hack of government administrative email system
date_note: Date of the ministry's release; the ministry says it was notified of the hack on 9 November.
org: Ministry of the Interior and Safety / National Information Resources Service
summary: South Korea's Interior Ministry says related agencies told it on 9 November that the administrative email system had been hacked. It says about 300 accounts showed abnormal access. The attacker entered through the weak network of some local governments and used a single sign-on flaw. The ministry reported the leak to the privacy regulator, notified those affected and began a joint inspection with the NIS and KISA.
plain: Hackers got into South Korean government work email accounts through a login flaw. The ministry has cut connections, told the people affected and is investigating.
exec: Shows how a weak local network and shared single sign-on can expose a national government system.
action: Review single sign-on and the links between partner or local networks and your email system; look for abnormal sign-ins.

sources.name: Ministry of the Interior and Safety (korea.kr)

validation.note: Government press release (primary source); the attacker is not named.
